locator: The whole photograph: the house's street front square to the camera behind three street trees, its full-width veranda with the stair at the north end, the two storeys of windows over it, the bracketed cornice and the mansard with its dormers; a lower set-back front to the left; J. P. Smith & Co.'s ice wagon at the curb on the right.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction with no rights statement (the Prairie library's ruling: 'unknown - link only'; the c. 1890 photograph is likely public domain by age, but its holder and the reproduction's terms are not established). Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-2933) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.

note: The only picture of 1736 Prairie this project reads. It shows the street front of a light-walled house two tall storeys over a raised basement: a veranda the front's whole width on four slender posts, a turned balustrade at the principal floor and a deep frieze under its roof, its stair rising at the north end between cheek walls; three windows in the upper storey under arched heads and eared hoods; a bracketed cornice; a steep mansard with two round-headed dormers on the street face; and a low pale wall along the street line. Left of the front, behind a tree, stands a lower front set back about 3 m with a one-storey canted bay and a dormer over it, which the 1911 sheet does not draw at 1736 (data/reference_views/house_1736_prairie/mcbirney_c1890_photo.match.json weighs it). It is evidence of c. 1890, not of 1904.
